forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: gets() performs no bounds checking and always causes a buffer overflow vulnerability.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace gets() with fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), stdin) which enforces a maximum read length.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: strcpy() performs no bounds checking and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace strcpy() with strlcpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) or strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)-1) with explicit null-termination.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: strcat() performs no bounds checking and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace strcat() with strlcat(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) or strncat(dst, src, sizeof(dst)-strlen(dst)-1).

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: sprintf() performs no bounds checking on the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace sprintf() with snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), ...) which enforces a maximum output length.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-120: vsprintf() performs no bounds checking on the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace vsprintf() with vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, args).

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG: system() invokes a shell and is vulnerable to command injection.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace system() with execve() using an explicit argument array and validated, absolute paths for the executable.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A03 / DISA STIG: popen() invokes a shell and is vulnerable to command injection via the command string.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use pipe() + fork() + execve() to create a child process without shell interpretation.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-90A: rand() is not cryptographically secure and must not be used for security operations.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Use /dev/urandom via getrandom(2) or a FIPS-validated DRBG from OpenSSL (RAND_bytes()) for security-sensitive randomness.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / STIG V-222645: MD5 is cryptographically broken and not FIPS-compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA-256 (SHA256_Init/SHA256_Update/SHA256_Final) or EVP_sha256() via OpenSSL EVP interface.

forbidden_patterns.reason: FIPS 140-3 / NIST SP 800-131A: SHA-1 is deprecated and not FIPS 140-3 compliant.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with SHA-256 (EVP_sha256()) or stronger via the OpenSSL EVP interface.

forbidden_patterns.reason: OWASP A07 / NIST IA-5: Hardcoded password detected in C source.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords. Read credentials from secure configuration files with restricted permissions or environment variables.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-252 / OWASP A05: Unchecked malloc() return value — NULL pointer dereference on allocation failure.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always check malloc() return value: ptr = malloc(size); if (!ptr) { /* handle error */ }

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG / CWE-120: scanf() with %s performs no bounds checking and can overflow the destination buffer.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace with scanf("%Ns", buf) specifying a maximum width (N = buffer size - 1), or use fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), stdin) for safer input.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-663 / POSIX: strtok() uses internal static state and is not thread-safe, causing data races in multi-threaded programs.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace strtok() with strtok_r(str, delim, &saveptr) (POSIX) or strtok_s() (C11 Annex K) which are reentrant and thread-safe.

forbidden_patterns.reason: CWE-190 / CWE-252: atoi() provides no error detection for invalid input or integer overflow — silently returns 0 for invalid input.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Replace atoi() with strtol(str, &endptr, 10) and validate endptr, errno, and the numeric range to properly handle conversion errors.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to printf() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always pass a string literal as the format argument: use printf("%s", user_input) not printf(user_input). Never let user-controlled data be interpreted as a format string.

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to fprintf() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always pass a string literal as the format argument: use fprintf(stream, "%s", user_input) not fprintf(stream, user_input).

forbidden_patterns.reason: DISA STIG APSC-DV-002560 / CWE-134: Passing a non-literal format argument to syslog() enables format string attacks — attackers can read memory, overwrite addresses, or crash the program.
forbidden_patterns.remediation: Always pass a string literal as the format argument: use syslog(priority, "%s", user_input) not syslog(priority, user_input).
